pattern: lead delegates a code change by role
experience: A Code lead asked for a change must hand it to a worker by role, name no model, and not edit the files itself.
rule: Never name a model, provider or effort in `target`. Code changes go to a Code worker: delegate_task with role implementation (or test). Do not edit files yourself.

pattern: user names a model; the lead still names none
experience: The user asks for a specific cheap model for the worker. The lead cannot choose a worker's model: whatever it names is ignored, so it must delegate without naming one.
rule: Each worker runs on the model set for its mode, and anything you name is ignored.

pattern: a lead starts a loop on another thread
experience: A lead cannot start loops (they are refused for it), so multi-round work goes to workers with delegate_task, fixes sent back to a worker.
rule: Do not start loops, schedule tasks or message other threads: those are refused for a lead. For work that needs several rounds, send fixes back to a worker.

experience: When delegate_task is refused for the live-worker cap, the lead must tell the person or wait for a worker, not do the work itself.
rule: If delegate_task is refused (a cap or a usage limit), tell the person why instead of doing the work yourself.

pattern: switching sub-agents on for another idle thread
experience: Asked to turn sub-agents on for another idle thread, the agent uses t3_sub_agents_set on that thread, and does not send it a message asking it to do so itself.
rule: t3_sub_agents_set: Turn sub-agents on or off for another idle thread. Not for your own thread or the lead you work for.
